pr.title: Select console sessions and panel items with the mouse
pr.head: 9e256e303cd02bb8507f07b1ca9778551fa9fdd5

summary: The Projector console lists agent sessions above the selected session’s pull requests, artifacts, and inbox items. This change lets you select those rows and use their drawer controls with a left click, alongside the existing keyboard navigation.

Each displayed click target keeps its session, row, and action attached. The terminal maps mouse coordinates to the visible frame; the console then applies its existing note fields, confirmations, and revision checks. Active text fields ignore clicks until you finish or cancel them.

cards.title: What a click does
cards.html:
• Click a session row to select it.
  • Click a panel row to open or close its drawer.
  • Click a choice to open its optional note field, or an action to use its normal confirmation.
  • Use the terminal’s mouse override when selecting text to copy.

cards.title: Verified on this head
cards.html:
• Clean review with no findings, suggestions, or follow-ups.
  • All 102 focused Python tests and 270 hook tests passed.
  • The configured validation gate and required CI check passed.
  • The pseudo-terminal regression sent native mouse reports through the actual CLI and verified the recorded answer.

groups.title: Route clicks through existing actions
groups.kicker: The rendered frame carries clickable rows and controls.
intro: A click target combines a session identity with an optional panel row and drawer action. Keeping that identity in the displayed frame prevents a refresh from turning an old click into an action on another session’s same-numbered inbox item.

The terminal records the targets after both panes have been scrolled and clipped, then adjusts them for its left padding. Only left clicks on those regions are handled. A resize invalidates old coordinates until the next draw, and terminals without mouse support keep keyboard navigation.

The console executes the captured action through the same path as a key press. Existing confirmation and optional-note behavior stays in that path; a choice captured before a question revision is still checked against the stored question before an answer is recorded.

files.note: Attach session-aware targets to rendered lines and dispatch terminal mouse events through the existing console actions.

checks.text: Focused tests confirmed that clicks preserve active notes and ignore targets whose session has disappeared.
Scroll and resize regressions passed: targets follow the visible viewport, and coordinates from a prior terminal size are ignored.

files.note: Document clickable rows and controls, active-field behavior, and the terminal override used to select text.

checks.text: Mouse support is an additional input path. Keyboard navigation, optional notes, and dismissal confirmations retain their existing behavior.

groups.title: Exercise clicks at model and terminal boundaries
groups.kicker: Regressions cover identity, layout changes, and real mouse reports.
intro: The model tests click positions from a displayed frame and assert on recorded inbox or subscription state. They cover correct-session answers, dismissal confirmation, both panes after scrolling, noninteractive areas, other buttons, active notes, removed sessions, terminal resize, and revised choices.
A pseudo-terminal test also launches the actual CLI and sends its terminal’s native mouse encoding. This checks the curses input boundary rather than relying only on simulated console callbacks.

files.note: Drive displayed targets with mouse events and verify the actual CLI accepts native mouse reports.

checks.text: The stale-choice test passed: a question revised after drawing is not answered by the old displayed choice, and the console reports the revision refusal.
The native mouse-report regression passed within the 102-test focused run, recording only the clicked answer and exiting without a traceback.
